title: Russell Brand trial for rape and sexual assault begins – live updates
summary:
Russell Brand back in Southwark Crown Court today where his rape and sexual assault trial is set to begin

30m agoRussell Brand rape and sexual assault trial begins

blocks.text: Brand was driven to the court in a black Mercedes-Benz van, which parked directly outside the court building, where crowds of reporters and photographers had gathered ahead of his trial.

Brand waited inside the vehicle for around a minute before stepping out, wearing a dark suit, a black and white striped shirt, a long white tie and sunglasses. He reached out for his wife’s hand before the pair walked together towards the court.
Brand arrives at court, says he feels 'concerned but hopeful'
Russell Brand spoke to the media as he arrived at court this morning, saying he was feeling “concerned but hopeful”.
He said: “Today I feel blessed, I feel of course concerned but hopeful that this process will lead to good outcomes for everybody involved.
Russell Brand rape and sexual assault trial begins
Russell Brand will be back in Southwark Crown Court today where his rape and sexual assault trial is expected to begin.

We should be hearing opening statements from the prosecution, which will set out an overview of the allegations against the 51-year-old comedian. He has been charged with three counts of rape, three of sexual assault and one of indecent assault against six women, in allegations that date from 1999 to 2009. Brand has pleaded not guilty to all the charges.
He has been pictured arriving at court this morning with his wife, Laura Gallacher.

blocks.caption: Russell Brand arrives at Southwark Crown Court on Wednesday. Photograph: Ben Whitley/PA

The Press Association has been outside court this morning, where news crews have been setting up shop several hours before the trial begins. Here’s what the news agency reports:

double quotation markA crowd of members of the press were gathered outside Southwark Crown Court hours before Russell Brand’s trial was due to start. Photographers, video journalists and news presenters could be seen in position at around 7.30am, while a line of reporters waited to get in to the court building. Members of court security were also outside the building, along with a small group of police officers. One police officer was heard telling members of the press to stay behind barriers which were in place directly outside the building.”
The trial is scheduled to begin at 10am, so follow along for live updates throughout the day as the case gets under way.
